text: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu each took his censer, put fire in it, laid incense on it, and offered unauthorized fire before the LORD, which he had not commanded them.
Then fire went out from before the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD.
Moses said to Aaron, "This is what the LORD meant when he said: 'Among those who draw near to me I will show myself holy, and before all the people I will be glorified.'" And Aaron was silent.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Uzziel, Aaron's uncle, and said to them, "Come here, carry your brothers away from the front of the sanctuary, outside the camp."
So they came and carried them, still in their tunics, outside the camp, as Moses had said.

Then Moses said to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Do not let your hair hang loose, and do not tear your garments, or you will die and wrath will come upon the whole congregation. But your brothers, the whole house of Israel, may mourn the burning that the LORD has kindled.
Do not leave the entrance of the tent of meeting, or you will die, for the LORD's anointing oil is upon you." And they did as Moses said.
The LORD spoke to Aaron:
"You and your sons with you are not to drink wine or strong drink when you enter the tent of meeting, or you will die. This is a lasting statute through all your generations,
so that you can distinguish between the holy and the common, between the unclean and the clean,
and so that you can teach the Israelites all the statutes that the LORD has spoken to them through Moses."

Moses said to Aaron and to his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, "Take the grain offering that is left from the food offerings of the LORD and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for it is most holy.
You must eat it in a holy place, because it is your portion and your sons' portion from the food offerings of the LORD; this is what I was commanded.

But the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution you may eat in a clean place, you and your sons and your daughters with you, for they are given as your portion and your sons' portion from the fellowship sacrifices of the Israelites.

They are to bring the thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering along with the food offerings of the fat portions, to wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. It will belong to you and your sons with you as a lasting portion, just as the LORD has commanded."
Then Moses made careful inquiry about the goat of the sin offering, and there it was—burned up! He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's remaining sons, and said,

versions.text: Then Moses searched carefully for the goat of the sin offering, and there it was—burned up! He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's remaining sons, and said,
versions.explanation: "Searched carefully for" suggests the goat was lost and Moses was hunting for it. The doubled verb דָּרֹשׁ דָּרַשׁ here means to inquire into or investigate the matter of the offering, which fits the following rebuke better and reads just as smoothly aloud.

text: "Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place? It is most holy, and the LORD gave it to you to take away the guilt of the congregation, to make atonement for them before the LORD.

versions.text: "Why did you not eat the sin offering in the sanctuary area? It is most holy, and he gave it to you to take away the guilt of the congregation, to make atonement for them before the LORD.
versions.explanation: "Sanctuary area" is vague and inconsistent with "a holy place" in v.13 and "the sanctuary" in v.18; "the holy place" renders מְקוֹם הַקֹּדֶשׁ directly. Also, naming the subject of "gave" removes the ambiguity of the bare pronoun "he" for a listener.

text: Look, its blood was not brought inside the holy place. You should certainly have eaten it in the holy place, as I commanded."

versions.text: Look, its blood was not brought inside the sanctuary. You should certainly have eaten it in the sanctuary, as I commanded."
versions.explanation: For consistency with the rendering of הַקֹּדֶשׁ elsewhere in the chapter, and to avoid the repetition of "sanctuary" in two different senses within one verse, "holy place" is clearer when read aloud.

text: Aaron said to Moses, "Look, today they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, and things like these have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would that have been good in the LORD's eyes?"
When Moses heard this, it seemed good to him.
